text:
jess: Heads-up — Customer X asked if we can do a tiny on‑prem POC with USB-delivered minibundles instead of full images. They're airgapped and want strict upgrade windows.
omar: Do we have a recommended minibundle strategy? i.e., what we can sign and delta-patch offline.
lia: yes — minibundle = model weights (quantized), runtime diffs, and a small operator. Signed manifest + SBOM. Keeps USB size small.
jess: They want upgrades only during monthly maintenance windows and no automatic egress. Also: HSM/KMS key custody question from security team.
tal: For keys: we support offline signing via customer HSM or we can provide a signed artifact if they accept escrow. Prefer customer-managed HSM for compliance.
omar: Pricing ask from procurement: is there a different license or per-device fee for minibundle distribution vs standard private? they want cost predictability.
lia: Sales note: minibundles are included under Private license but offline support + extended SLAs are an add-on. We usually quote a per-device provisioning fee + yearly support band.
ops-bot: Deploy checklist:
- verify host os packages
- install operator v1.12
- import signed-manifest.json
- run: ./redwood-install --bundle path/to/minibundle.tar.gz --offline

jess: Customer asked about delta updates (patch-only USB). Can we support incremental patching so they don't have to reimage every time?
tal: Yes — operator supports chunked delta application. You ship a signed patch manifest referencing previous bundle sha256. We verify chain-of-trust via customer root CA.
omar: Security Q: they asked to see fields from our questionnaire about SBOM, runtime telemetry, and crypto algorithms.
lia: Reply for questionnaire:
- SBOM: provided per-bundle in SPDX format
- Telemetry: opt-in; agent offline mode disables telemetry and logs locally
- Crypto: RSA-2048 for signing, HKDF + AES-GCM for envelope; HSM integrations: PKCS#11 supported
jess: How do we handle forced rollback if a minibundle fails in staging? they want a safe fallback path.
tal: Operator keeps previous runtime + model snapshot for N=2 rollbacks. Fallback is instantaneous if health checks fail within 5 minutes.
omar: Can we deliver quantized model variants in the minibundle to keep size < 8GB? they asked specifically for int8.
lia: Yes — we produce q4/q8 bundles. We include a small compatibility matrix in the manifest so operator picks right binary.
jess: They also want the upgrade cadence locked to quarterly main releases and emergency patches only. Is that supported?
tal: Supported. We can tag builds as `quarterly` vs `hotfix`. Hotfixes require signed approval and are shipped as delta bundles; customer can restrict install to approved tokens.
omar: Any docs/snippet I can forward?
lia: Paste manifest example:
{  "bundle": "minibundle-2026-03-01.tar.gz",  "sha256": "abc123...",  "components": ["runtime:1.12","model:q8-bert-2026-02"],  "signature": "base64sig...",  "compat": ["ubuntu-22.04","centos-8"],  "upgrade_channel": "quarterly" }
jess: Great. Omar — can you ask procurement what flat provisioning budget they expect? I'll draft the security reply and ops checklist.
omar: Will do. Looping in legal later for escrow options. Thanks team :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Note: File upload policy — USB bundles must be scanned and checksummed on ingestion.
lia: I'll prepare a short POC runbook and a pricing delta estimate (provisioning + 12-month support). Expect a draft by EOD PST.
jess: Perfect. If procurement asks for discounts for multi-site, we offer tiered provisioning credits (e.g., 10 devices = 1 free, 50+ = custom).
omar: Filing request with procurement now. Closing loop once I have budget number.
